# Lab 2: RStudio Projects and Quarto Documents

## Learning Objectives
* Create an **RStudio Project** to organize your work.
* Understand the structure of a **Quarto (.qmd)** document.
* "Render" a quarto document into a professional HTML report.

---

## Part 1: RStudio Projects
In Data Science, organization is everything. An RStudio Project keeps your code, data, and images in one "folder" so R always knows where to look.

::: {.callout-important}
## 📝 Lab Task 1: Setting Up Your Workspace

Before writing any code, you must organize your environment. Follow these steps to create your project structure:

### Step 1: Create the RStudio Project
1. Open **RStudio**.
2. In the top menu, click **File > New Project…**
3. Select **New Directory** > **New Project**.
4. **Directory Name:** Type `MAT186_Labs`.
5. **Create project as subdirectory of:** Click *Browse* and select your **Documents** folder.
6. Click **Create Project**.

## Step 2: Create Professional Sub-folders

Data scientists never leave files "floating" in the main folder. Use the **Files pane** (bottom-right window) to create a professional structure:

1. Click the **New Folder** button.
2. Type `data` and click **OK**. (This is where you will save datasets).
3. Click the **New Folder** button again.
4. Type `images` and click **OK**. (This is where you will save plots and graphs).
5. Click the **New Folder** button again.
6. Type `Lab_solutions` and click **OK**. (This is your master folder for the entire semester).
7. **Important:** In the Files pane, click on the `Lab_solutions` folder to enter it.
8. While inside `Lab_solutions`, click the **New Folder** button one last time.
9. Type `Lab02_yourname` and click **OK**.

## Step 3: Verification & Submission
To verify your setup, take a **screenshot** of your RStudio interface. 

**Your screenshot must clearly show:**
1. The project name `MAT186_Labs` in the top-right corner of RStudio.
2. The `data` and `images` folders in the **Files** pane (bottom-right).
* The `Lab02_yourname` folder nested inside `Lab_solutions` in the Files pane.

Save this as `lab02_task1.png` on your `Lab02_yourname` folder.
:::





::: {.callout-note}
### Why do this?
By creating these now, you are ready for Lab 5! You will put all your datasets in `/data` and all your plots/diagrams in `/images`.
:::

## Part 2: Creating a Quarto Document

# Lab 2: Introduction to Quarto

Quarto allows you to combine text, code, and results into one professional document. Follow these steps to get started.

## Creating your Document

1.  In the top menu, click **File > New File > Quarto Document...**
2.  Title it **"Lab 2"** and put your name as the **Author**.
3.  Click **Create**. It will open a quarto document.

---

## The Three Parts of a Quarto Document

A Quarto document is made of three distinct components:

### 1. The YAML Header
Look at the very top of the file. You will see text between two sets of three dashes (`---`). This is the **YAML Header**; it contains the "metadata" or settings for your document.

```yaml
---
title: "Lab 2"
author: "Your Name"
format: html
editor: visual
---
```



### 2. Markdown (Narrative)
The plain white areas of the document are called **Markdown**. This is where you write your analysis, explain your results, and answer questions. It works like a simplified word processor.

* You can make text **bold** by using `**double asterisks**`.
* You can make text *italic* by using `*single asterisks*`.

### 3. Code Chunks
The gray boxes starting with ` ```{r} ` and ending with ` ``` ` are called **Code Chunks**. This is where you put your R code to run calculations or create graphs.

```{r}
#| label: example-chunk
# This is a code chunk. R code goes here!
1 + 1
```



::: {.callout-note}
## Tip for Students
To run the code inside a chunk, click the green **Play** button in the top-right corner of the gray box. The result will appear directly below the chunk!
:::


---

## Part 3: Rendering (The "Magic" Button)
To turn your code into a report:

1. Click the **Render** button (blue arrow icon) at the top of the editor.
2. RStudio will save the file and pop up a beautiful HTML window.

---

::: {.callout-important}
## 📝 Lab Task 2: Your First Calculation in a quarto document

Follow these steps to practice using Quarto:

1.  **Create a Document**: In RStudio, go to **File > New File > Quarto Document**. Name it `Lab2_task2_yourname`.
2.  **Clean the Workspace**: Find the heading that says **Quarto**. Delete all the example text and code *below* that line so you have a blank white space.
3.  **Add a Title**: In that new blank area, type a title for your work: `# Lab 2`. 
    *(Note: Using the # symbol makes the text large like a heading!)*
4.  **Insert a Chunk**: Click the **+C** button to create a new gray R chunk. Inside the chunk, type: `2 + 2`
   
5.  **Render the Report**: Click the **Render** button (blue arrow icon) at the top of your screen. 
6.  **Check Results**: Look at your final HTML report. You should see your title **Lab 2**, the code `2 + 2`, and the result `4`.
7.  **Submit**: upload your HTML report in Brightspace and submit it.
:::

2. Select the correct Lab folder.
3. Upload your **.zip** file and click **Submit**.
